behavioral_notes.observation: When publisher_comment is set during create or write, the module auto-fills publisher_id (current user's partner) and publisher_datetime (Datetime.now()) if not already supplied. Before persisting, _check_synchronize_publisher_values enforces dual-path authorization: either the user holds website.group_website_restricted_editor (resolved via ir.model.data._xmlid_to_res_id to avoid a hard bridge dependency) OR they have write access on the rated document (checked via records.check_access('write')). Metadata shows only field definitions, not this gating behavior.

When rating_include=True is in options, _portal_message_format performs a sudo search_read on rating.rating filtered by message_id, then injects a rating_id dict per message (publisher_comment, publisher_id, publisher_datetime formatted via format_datetime, publisher_avatar URL as /web/image/res.partner/<id>/avatar_128/50x50). It also calls rating_get_stats() on the related document model if that method exists, attaching aggregate stats as rating_stats. This enrichment is a runtime injection invisible in ORM metadata.

portal_rating extends PortalChatter: _get_non_empty_message_domain adds Domain('rating_value', '!=', False) via OR so that messages containing only a rating (no text body) are still shown in the chatter. _setup_portal_message_fetch_extra_domain accepts an optional rating_value float from the client and appends an AND Domain filter, enabling server-side star-rating-filtered chatter views without any dedicated filter model.

The frontend Thread model patch unconditionally adds rating_include=true to all chatter fetch params for non-discuss.channel threads, and also forwards rating_value when a star filter is active (this.selectedRating). This drives the server-side rating enrichment on every portal chatter load — the metadata-level Module has no OWL components; all behavior is delivered through patches on existing components.

The RatingPopupComposer Interaction renders a star average widget (portal_rating.rating_stars_static template) and a modal wrapping the portal.Composer. On reload (triggered by bus event reload_rating_popup_composer), it merges returned mail.thread rating_avg/rating_count and rating.rating rating values back into options, changing the send button label to 'Update review' vs 'Post review' depending on whether default_message_id is set. Access token (token field) is passed through options from the server-rendered page.

it_architecture.application: portal_rating (bridge: exposes rating.rating publisher comments and aggregate stats in the customer portal chatter)
data_objects: mail.message (extended: rating payload injected into portal format at runtime)
logical_data_erm: rating.rating -> <any rated document model> (write-access check via _classify_by_model)
information_flows: portal chatter fetch -> Thread.getFetchParams injects rating_include=true -> mail.message._portal_message_format enriches payload with rating_id + rating_stats
portal user POSTs /website/rating/comment -> rating.rating.write (access-gated) -> returns formatted publisher block to frontend
frontend_components: RatingPopupComposer (public.interactions — star popup + portal composer modal)
Patches: Thread, Chatter, Composer, Message, PortalComposer, Store

capabilities: Display customer star ratings with aggregate average and count in portal chatter
Allow portal users to post and edit rating reviews (star + text via portal composer)
Allow publishers (website editors or document owners) to respond to ratings with a comment
Filter portal chatter messages by exact star rating value (server-side domain filter)
value_streams: Customer Feedback Loop: customer submits star rating via portal -> publisher sees rating in chatter with aggregate stats -> publisher posts response comment -> customer sees response and updated stats on portal
information_concepts: mail.message (chatter message linked to rating via message_id)
policies: Publisher comment write requires either website.group_website_restricted_editor membership OR write access on the rated document (dual-path guard in _check_synchronize_publisher_values — bridge to website is optional, not a hard dependency)
stakeholders: Customer (portal user submitting rating via RatingPopupComposer)
Publisher / Document Owner (res.users with write access on rated record)
metrics: rating_avg and rating_count per document (surfaced via rating_get_stats in portal chatter payload)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: portal_rating enables bilateral communication between customers and businesses around service/product ratings — a network value model where value lies in connecting reviewers with publishers. It supports the Market & Sell process by surfacing customer satisfaction signals in the portal, helping prospects assess quality and letting businesses respond publicly.

standard_capabilities: Star rating display with average and count in portal chatter
Rating-filtered chatter (client-side star filter drives server domain)
Publisher response comments with auto-stamped identity and timestamp
RatingPopupComposer widget for submitting/editing portal reviews
Translation support via ir.http frontend module registration
typical_fits: Any module using mail.thread rating mixin automatically gains portal rating display
Publisher comment fields auto-populated (user, datetime) on write — no manual tracking needed
Optional bridge to website.group_website_restricted_editor — works without website module
common_gaps: No moderation workflow (approve/reject ratings before publication)
No separate review model — publisher comment fields tightly coupled to rating.rating
No notification to publisher when a new rating arrives (relies on upstream rating module events)
drive_hints: curl jsonrpc /website/rating/comment with auth=user session, body: {rating_id: <id>, publisher_comment: '...'}

open_questions: Does portal_rating interact with website live-chat or helpdesk rating flows, or only with modules that explicitly implement rating_get_stats?
Is the RatingPopupComposer access token (options.token) validated server-side by the upstream rating module, or is authentication solely by user session?
How does the frontend star-filter (rating_value param in Thread.getFetchParams) interact with pagination on large chatter threads — does the count reflect the filtered subset?
